lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5 you met roots like photo (light) and graph (write or draw). So what is a photograph? A picture drawn with light.
Greek and Latin affixes and roots help you unlock hard words. Split a long word into its parts, work out each part, then put the meaning back together.
Roots: audi (hear), bene (good), chron (time), cred (believe), ject (throw), log (word or study), vid and vis (see).
Prefixes: anti- (against), inter- (between), sub- (under), trans- (across), bi- (two). Suffixes: -ology (study of), -ible (can be), -ist (a person who).
Put them together: chronology = time + study of: the order of events in time. Incredible = in (not) + cred (believe) + ible (can be): hard to believe.
Try it in the world: invent a name for a new gadget in your world from roots, like a "chrono-lamp" that shows the time. Explain it to a friend. Next: personification and other figures of speech.

exercises.hint: Think of audience.
exercises.explain: audi means hear: an audience hears a show.

exercises.hint: Think of submarine.
exercises.explain: sub- means under: a submarine goes under the sea.

exercises.hint: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
exercises.explain: Yes: bi- means two.

exercises.hint: Think of chronicle.
exercises.explain: chron means time: a chronicle tells events in time order.

exercises.hint: Think of artist.
exercises.explain: -ist means a person who.

exercises.hint: Split it: audi (hear) + ible (can be). Put the meanings together.
exercises.explain: audible: can be heard.

exercises.hint: sub (under) + marine (sea).
choices: a boat that goes under the sea
exercises.explain: A submarine goes under the sea.

exercises.hint: Put trans- (across) in front of the ocean's name.
exercises.explain: Transatlantic: across the Atlantic.

exercises.hint: in (not) + cred (believe) + ible.
exercises.explain: Yes: it can hardly be believed.

exercises.hint: bio (life) + log (study) + ist.
exercises.explain: A biologist studies living things.

exercises.hint: e- means out.
exercises.explain: Eject: e- (out) + ject (throw): to throw out.

exercises.prompt: "Bene" means good. What is a benefit?
exercises.hint: Think of "beneficial": is it good or bad for you?
exercises.explain: A benefit is something good.

exercises.hint: chron means time.
exercises.explain: Chronological order is the order things happened.

exercises.hint: inter- means between.
exercises.explain: Yes: inter- means between.

exercises.prompt: "Vis" means see and "-ible" means can be. What does "invisible" mean?
exercises.hint: in- means not.
exercises.explain: Invisible: cannot be seen.

exercises.prompt: Match each word part to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Think of a word for each: antibiotic, international, chronicle, credible, biology.
exercises.explain: anti-: against. inter-: between. chron: time. cred: believe. -ology: study of.

exercises.prompt: Sort the words by the meaning of their root.
exercises.hint: Find vid or vis, audi, or cred inside each word.
exercises.explain: Video and visible have vid and vis (see). Audible and audience have audi (hear). Credit and incredible have cred (believe).

exercises.prompt: Sort the words by what their prefix means.
exercises.hint: Find anti-, inter- or sub- at the start of each word.
exercises.explain: Anti- means against: antibiotic, anticlockwise. Inter- means between: international, interval. Sub- means under: subway, submerge.

exercises.prompt: Build the word for "a person who studies living things": put the parts in order.
exercises.hint: Life comes first, then the study part, then the person.
exercises.explain: bio (life) + log (study) + ist (a person who) makes biologist: a person who studies living things.

exercises.prompt: How many word parts are in "inaudible"?
exercises.hint: Look for a prefix, a root and a suffix you know.
exercises.explain: in (not) + aud (hear) + ible (can be): 3 parts. Inaudible means it cannot be heard.

exercises.prompt: Split each word into its parts, then match it to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Find the root you know in each word: bene, port, chron, ject.
exercises.explain: Benefactor: bene (good), someone who does good by giving. Transport: trans (across) + port (carry). Chronometer: chron (time), a clock that measures it. Projectile: ject (throw), something thrown forward.

exercises.prompt: Match each prefix to a word that uses it.
exercises.hint: Look at the start of each word on the right.
exercises.explain: anti-: antifreeze (against freezing). inter-: internet (between networks). sub-: submarine (under the sea). trans-: transatlantic (across the Atlantic). bi-: bicycle (two wheels).
